citation: Torchio et al. (2016). LIONSIMBA: A Matlab framework based on a finite volume model suitable for Li-ion battery design, simulation, and control. Journal of The Electrochemical Society 163(7), A1192–A1205.
description: LIONSIMBA is a MATLAB toolbox developed by Torchio, Magni, Gopaluni, Braatz, Raimondo and collaborators for lithium-ion battery design, simulation and control. A finite-volume formulation represents battery dynamics, with current or power profiles, thermal modelling and state-of-charge initialisation options. Inputs are cell parameters and operating profiles; outputs are simulated electrochemical and thermal states over a user-selected experiment. Coverage is global at cell or multicell level, without a fixed observed dataset. Public source is free under MIT, and the documented version 2.1 adds Octave support; MATLAB has separate commercial terms. A limitation is that the README reports numerical differences between thermal configurations and state-of-charge initialisation methods, and labels a spectral diffusion scheme as beta. It also records a correction to an equation in the describing paper. The toolbox can support battery-component and storage-control studies, complementary to system-level PyPSA (model-pypsa). The 2016 Journal of The Electrochemical Society article identifies the method. No battery simulation was run or article PDF downloaded.
name: LIONSIMBA lithium-ion battery toolbox
